instruction: The middleware package's `XxxWithConfig(config XxxConfig) echo.MiddlewareFunc` constructors panic on an invalid configuration, so a misconfigured middleware brings the whole server down at startup. Change every one of them -- `BasicAuthWithConfig`, `BodyDumpWithConfig`, `BodyLimitWithConfig`, `GzipWithConfig`, `ContextTimeoutWithConfig`, `CORSWithConfig`, `CSRFWithConfig`, `DecompressWithConfig`, `KeyAuthWithConfig`, `MethodOverrideWithConfig`, `ProxyWithConfig`, `RateLimiterWithConfig`, `RecoverWithConfig`, the five `...RedirectWithConfig` constructors, `RequestIDWithConfig`, `RequestLoggerWithConfig`, `RewriteWithConfig`, `SecureWithConfig`, `AddTrailingSlashWithConfig`, `RemoveTrailingSlashWithConfig` and `StaticWithConfig` -- to return `(echo.MiddlewareFunc, error)`, i.e. the result of `config.ToMiddleware()`, instead of panicking. The convenience constructors without a config (`BasicAuth(fn)`, `CORS(...)`, `Gzip()`, `Proxy(b)`, `HTTPSRedirect()`, `Static(root)`, ...) keep returning a bare `echo.MiddlewareFunc` and keep panicking on invalid input: they call the `...WithConfig` function and panic with its non-nil error. Update every other caller of a `...WithConfig` middleware constructor (all of them are tests): bind both results (`mw, err := ...`) and check the error with `require.NoError(t, err)` using the test's `*testing.T`/`*testing.B` before using the middleware (in a function without one, panic on a non-nil error); a call nested inside another expression (`e.Use(CORSWithConfig(cfg))`, `RewriteWithConfig(cfg)(handler)`, a struct field) must be hoisted into its own statement just before the statement that uses it. Tests that asserted a constructor panics (`assert.Panics(t, func() { XxxWithConfig(bad) })`) must instead assert the returned error (`assert.Error`), and `assert.NotPanics` around a constructor becomes `assert.NoError` on its error; panic assertions about the convenience constructors and about running a handler stay. Do not change `echo.NewWithConfig`, `NewRateLimiterMemoryStoreWithConfig` or the `ToMiddleware` methods, and do not add `Must...` helpers or other wrappers. Behavior of valid configurations must not change.
gold_tool: build_deep.py deephard go recipe: declarations + wrapper returns by pattern; (Not)Panics assertions around a constructor rewritten to error assertions; every remaining caller hoisted with go/ast statement positions (deephard_astq.go) and checked with the enclosing test's require.NoError, driven by go build/go test compile errors; gofmt (go1.25)
change: change 25 constructors' result T -> (T, error); wrappers switch to the panicking helper, every other call is hoisted out of its expression and error-checked with the in-scope *testing.T; panic/no-panic assertions become error assertions
notes: Call contexts: e.Use(X(cfg)), e.Pre(X(cfg)), X(cfg)(handler)(c), mw := X(cfg), table-driven subtests (t from the t.Run closure), benchmarks (*testing.B), assert.Panics closures.
